title: A prospective observational study to evaluate biomarkers and disease mechanisms in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis with systemic therapy
summary:
Atopic dermatitis is one of the most common chronic inflammatory skin diseases. In addition to topical treatment, systemically administered immunosuppressants and in particular targeted therapeutics such as biologics and JAK inhibitors are playing an increasingly important role in therapy for moderate to severe forms. However, with all therapeutic options, only a proportion of patients show a sufficient response (sufficient improvement of clinical signs and symptoms, long-term control); moreover, the therapeutic response is unpredictable. Thus, it is unclear which patient will benefit most from which therapy.
The main purpose of this study is to identify new biomarkers for stratification of patients with atopic dermatitis that can predict response to specific therapeutics and map the degree of disease control during therapy. To this end, we would like to obtain additional biomaterials from patients undergoing systemic therapy as part of their routine care at routine visit time points (but without interfering with medical treatment or therapy decisions) and study them molecularly.
Potential study participants are patients with moderately to severely active atopic dermatitis who are prescribed a systemic therapy by their treating physician and are taking this therapy.

interventions.name:
Only one study arm

There are no study interventions as such.

Up to 50 ml of blood will be collected at the routine visits at week 0, week 2, week 12 and week 52 after initiation of a new system therapy for routine blood sampling at the center and patients will be asked to provide stool, urine

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Written informed consent from the study participant prior to performing any study-related activities.
2) Age ≥ 18 years at the time of study entry.
3) Clinically diagnosed atopic dermatitis.
4) Initiation of systemic therapy for atopic dermatitis by the treating physician as part of routine care
5) Study participant agrees and, in the judgment of study personnel, is able to comply with the study protocol for the duration of the study
Exclusion criteria:
1) Study participant is not capable of consenting to study participation or adhering to the study protocol.
2) Tendency to keloid/hypertrophic scarring and/or known wound healing disorder.
3) Tattooing and/or skin lesions due to a dermatosis in the puncture area not investigated in this study
4) Needle phobia
5) Pregnancy 
6) Liver/biliary tract disease present at the time of the study and judged unstable by the study physician, manifested by ascites, encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hypoalbuminemia, esophageal/gastric varices, persistent jaundice, and/or liver cir-rhosis
7) Known allergy and/or hypersensitivity to the materials used.
8) Any reason that, in the opinion of the study physician, may prevent safe participation of the study participant.
